papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by Garc\'ia-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

papers.title: Discrete history operators: Exact state-space realization for sequence memory
papers.abstract: A prescribed finite-dimensional analysis of an evolving discrete history need not admit an exact recurrence driven only by its current state and the entering input. We study exact realizations of causal linear discrete history operators (DHOs). Operator factorization and kernel inclusion characterize exact closure, while the cross-projection defect characterizes closure failure for orthonormal analyses. For finite-dimensional history spaces over fixed finite horizons, we distinguish two minimality problems. Reachable task quotients determine the minimum state dimension for preserving prescribed future tasks on reachable histories. Backward invariant envelopes characterize the minimum dimension of exact linear realizations recovering prescribed analyses on full history spaces within the admissible class. The minimum number of additional independent state directions is given by the rank of the propagated closure defect operator restricted to the kernel of the current analysis. For geometrically weighted countable histories, matrix mode transport yields structured exact recurrences and a uniform exponential decay estimate for state transitions. Additional conditions provide uniform Gram bounds and refined decay estimates. A stationary Meixner specialization yields explicit recurrence matrices, an O(N) arithmetic state update, and minimum augmentation dimensions over finite horizons for selected coefficients. Numerical experiments examine recurrence accuracy, state transition bounds, Gram conditions, and minimum realization dimensions.

papers.title: The fixed-point proportion of Lattès maps
papers.abstract: How often does an element of the geometric iterated Galois group of a Latt\`es map fix a vertex of the tree? Let A/K be an abelian variety over a separably closed field of characteristic 0, G <= Aut(A,0) finite, and alpha an isogeny of degree at least 2 normalising G. The Latt\`es map on X=A/G has a preimage tree governed by alpha-power torsion; we determine the fixed-point proportion in every dimension. For zeta in G the weight is the reciprocal of the number of fixed points of zeta in alpha-power torsion (zero if infinite); equivalently, it is a product of p-adic absolute values of determinants on the alpha-active subspaces; for scalar alpha=m the proportion is (1/|G|) times the sum over 1 != zeta in G of the product over p dividing m of the p-adic absolute value of det(1 - zeta | H_1(A,Z)). We deduce positivity and vanishing criteria, prove the groups G_infinity are martingale groups, determine the limit law, and reduce groups with translations to the fixed-origin case. In dimension one we determine ten values for scalar multipliers and nontrivial G <= Aut(E,0), and for the eight quadratic Latt\`es classes the proportions are 1/8, 1/4 and 5/16. Bridy-Jones-Kelsey-Lodge exclude the Latt\`es case from their main theorem; their Theorem 2.5 periodic-point bound is attained, via reductions modulo split primes p = 1 (mod 4), for the map (x^2+a)/(x^2-a), a^2 = -1, and we settle the exceptional case of the Fari\~na-Asategui-Radi conjecture.

papers.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of nonergodic directions in higher genus via effective equidistribution
papers.abstract: For each fixed $g\ge3$, we prove that non-uniquely ergodic directions have Hausdorff dimension $1/2$ on almost every area-one surface in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{odd}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is odd, and in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{nonhyp}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is even. We construct these directions through cyclic splittings into $g$ slit tori. Effective equidistribution of Lindenstrauss--Mohammadi--Yang supplies sufficiently many children at each normal input. We estimate cusp and periodic-orbit failures with the original branching weights and prove that their total mass loss is summable. The surviving path measure yields the dimension lower bound, also for directions nonergodic for flat area.

papers.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
papers.abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

papers.title: Hypercyclic and topologically transitive semigroups of composition operators (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a separable locally compact metric space, let $E\neq\{0\}$ be a normed space, and let $G$ be a semigroup of continuous self-maps of $X$. Every $\varphi\in G$ induces the composition operator $C_\varphi f=f\circ\varphi$ on the space $C(X,E)$ of continuous functions endowed with the compact-open topology. We characterize the topological transitivity of the semigroup $\widehat{G}=\{C_\varphi:\varphi\in G\}$ by a condition that combines the run-away property of $G$ with an approximate form of injectivity, and we show that, when $E$ is separable, $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive if and only if it is hypercyclic. In particular, if every element of $G$ is one-to-one and $G$ is run-away, then $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive, and hypercyclic when $E$ is separable. For a single map $\varphi$ we obtain: $C_\varphi$ is hypercyclic $\iff$ $C_\varphi$ is topologically transitive $\iff$ $\varphi$ is one-to-one and run-away, and $C_\varphi$ is mixing $\iff$ $\varphi$ is one-to-one and strongly run-away. If, moreover, $\varphi$ is an open map (which is automatic on manifolds by invariance of domain), then $C_\varphi$ is Devaney chaotic. On an open interval all of these properties are equivalent to $\varphi$ being one-to-one without fixed points.

papers.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two successive contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations in Katriel's differential-equation model, but no chaos. We derive from the elementary reactions of the process, without reference to the differential equations, a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_\tau$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_\tau$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. The chaotic attractor is essentially unique, with one positive Lyapunov exponent and an outbreak--recharge geometry. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is therefore not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.

papers.title: Modelling and analysis of a cocktail phage therapy with coinfection
papers.abstract: We analyze a delay differential model for phage therapy in which a cocktail of $n$ different types of bacteriophages, each with its own latency period, is administered and coinfection is allowed. We prove the global existence, uniqueness and nonnegativity of solutions, and the existence of an invariant region, under suitable conditions, in which the bacteria are eradicated exponentially fast. We determine the stability of the bacteria-free equilibrium in terms of the administered doses and give sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of coexistence equilibria, showing that coinfection may allow bacteria and phages to coexist even when the doses are large. For a cocktail of two phage types with the same latency period, we obtain a complete description of the biologically feasible coexistence equilibria, which may be zero, one or two. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichmüller Complex Manifold Structure
papers.abstract: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichm\"uller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichm\"uller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles. This connection allows us to establish asymptotic conformal rigidity for these dynamical quasicircles. Finally, we establish a foundation for the systematic study of the ergodic properties of geometric Gibbs measures.

papers.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-Følner sequences
papers.abstract: We study the quantity $\sup_{\phi\in\Phi}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\phi(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $\Phi$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $\Phi$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $\phi\in\Phi$ of the limit of $\phi(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``F{\o}lnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is F\o lner. A corollary of this result is that every choice of a non-F\o lner sequence overestimates topological and measure-theoretic entropy by the multiplicative factor $C(\mathcal F)$ (in the positive entropy case). We obtain a generalization of classical results of Goodman, Krug, and Newton, on the so-called proportionality principle for sequence entropy, and their extension by Gao, Huang, and Zhu to countable amenable groups.

papers.title: h-dichotomies via noncritical uniformity and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.

papers.title: Periodic counting, carry synchronization, and primes in nonstandard numeration systems
papers.abstract: Let $b\ge2$ be an integer and let $D\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ be a finite digit set containing zero, with maximum residue multiplicity $\mu=\max_{0\le r<b}\#\{d\in D:d\equiv r\pmod b\}$ and cardinality $q=\#D\ge2$. Under the condition $\mu<q$, we prove that the summatory representation function satisfies an asymptotic formula with a strictly positive, H\"older continuous, $1$-periodic fluctuating profile and an error of $O_D(x^{\log_b\mu})$. An exact periodic factorization of the Laplace generating function furnishes an explicit, computable Fourier expansion for the periodic profile via Gamma factors, and yields the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series to the entire complex plane. When $D$ is a complete residue system modulo $b$, we establish an arithmetic synchronization criterion showing that the associated finite carry system admits a zero-synchronizing word if and only if $\gcd(D)=1$. This synchronization yields an exponentially accurate interval approximation and a general transfer principle for arithmetic weights. Consequently, we derive a prime number theorem for representable primes governed by the same periodic profile, alongside an exponentially convergent measurable scaling limit of the representable sets.

papers.title: Multivariable Congruence Jumping: Periodic States, Integral Realizations, and Descent
papers.abstract: Congruence jumping replaces coordinates by integer quotients and updates polynomial divisibility relations. We extend this procedure to several variables and retain integer coefficients by recording their common factor separately. For three-variable systems of divisibilities with signed binomial numerators, we classify all positive integer exponent tuples of period at most two under three successive coordinate jumps: seven fixed tuples and twenty-two cycles of exact period two. No odd period greater than one occurs. At the chosen representatives of the twenty-two exponent two-cycles, there are eighty-four returning sign assignments. All have realizations with nonzero pairwise-coprime integer coordinates, and exactly seventy-four have such realizations with every coordinate positive throughout the six jumps. Explicit constructions and congruence arguments establish this classification. We also study jumps that decrease a specified height, distinguishing points that admit no immediate decrease from minima of entire connected components of the jump graph. For the four-variable family $Q_\lambda(x,y,z,w)=kxyzw$, where $Q_\lambda$ is the sum of the four squares plus $\lambda$ times the six pairwise products, finite bounds give complete classifications for $\lambda=1,2,3$. For $\lambda=1$, positive integer solutions exist exactly for $k=2,8,10$. These results distinguish returns of the polynomial data from integrality and positivity of the coordinate sequences.

papers.title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
papers.abstract: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I. Gringlaz, R. Kumar, B. Weiss. We also find the possible densities of the set of visible points in the cut-and-project set, with a constant generic lattice, and a changing window with constant volume. We also study bounds for the distance of large holes in the set of visible points of certain cut-and-project sets, generalizing theorems originally proved by P. Erd\H{o}s for $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
papers.abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
